source.title: Lifetimes of Rydberg levels in the perturbed 6snp 3P2 series of ytterbium I
source.version: published publisher layout with iText wrapper

coverage.coverageDefinition: All ten explicitly tabulated lifetime values and wave numbers, all numerical lifetime-related accuracy/check statements, and the qualitative scaling comparator are recorded; raw graph trace not digitized.
coverage.visualInspection: All3rendered PDF pages inspected, including Table I, Fig.3, Fig.4 and all IV(1)-(4) caveats.

experimentalConditions.sample: Neutral ytterbium atomic beam; isotope and hyperfine F not specified.
experimentalConditions.measurementMethod: Three-step pulsed-laser excitation followed by time-resolved fluorescence; repeated measurements fitted to a single exponential plus constant background.

environment.radiation: Room-temperature lifetime measurements as stated for Fig.4; exact wall temperature not reported.
environment.ovenTemperatureQualifier: about; this is source/atomic-beam temperature, not blackbody bath temperature

laser.geometry: Laser beams cross atomic beam at right angles; small mutual laser-beam angle about1mrad.

checks.name: blackbody radiation
checks.result: Surrounding the interaction region with a liquid-nitrogen-cooled trap changed lifetimes by an amount of the same order as experimental uncertainties.

checks.name: radiation trapping
checks.result: Density range checked and density kept low enough to avoid a large lifetime influence; no numerical density or correction provided.

checks.name: flight out of view
checks.result: Collection optics adjusted; authors estimate flight-out effect negligible for lifetimes shorter than3 microseconds. Exact3-microsecond entry is at the stated boundary, not a stricter bound.

checks.name: quantum beats
checks.result: Helmholtz field applied to make Zeeman beats faster than time resolution; no lifetime difference within error with/without field. Field magnitude not reported.

records.uncertaintyDescription: No per-entry uncertainty printed. Authors estimate about10% overall accuracy including statistical scatter and possible systematic errors; no1sigma interpretation is supplied.
records.definition: Single-exponential fluorescence decay time; paper labels Table I values as natural radiative lifetimes while Fig.4 and discussion identify room-temperature measurements with finite-temperature checks. Not a state-resolved decay branching fraction.

theoryComparisons.definition: Fig.4 includes a slope3 straight line for orientation; it is not a reported fit coefficient or a numerical MQDT prediction of these measured states.
Introduction cites theory for perturbed6snd singlet/triplet D2 series, which is different from the present6snp3P2 set. No numeric theory lifetime is supplied in this paper.

decayBranchingCoverage.boundary: Time-resolved fluorescence lifetimes alone do not determine a normalized state-resolved decay branching table.

pending.description: No isotope-resolved or hyperfine-resolved assignment is given; do not label these values171Yb or a particular F.
No tabulated blackbody-corrected0K lifetimes or per-state LN2/room-temperature differences.
Individual uncertainty bars/standard deviations and covariance are absent; overall10% accuracy cannot be silently assigned as per-point1sigma.
Effective principal quantum numbers are only graphical; no exact n* or quantum-defect table is reported. Do not infer precise numbers from graph positions.
Authors state interpretation using an odd-parity J=2 MQDT wave function is in progress; no fitted MQDT lifetimes or expansion coefficients are published here.
Helmholtz-field quantum-beat test lacks numerical field/time-resolution settings.
Text claims flight-out negligible for tau shorter than3microseconds; Table I16P2=3000ns is at the stated threshold. No correction magnitude is supplied.

adoptionPolicy: Evidence archive only. Does not modify canonical atomic lifetime, low-state decay branching, physics formulas, or main diagram.
